skill.name: convex-domains
skill.description: Connect a domain you own to Convex hosting or HTTP actions. Configure DNS records, verify HTTPS, and update the sign-in origin when needed.
skill.summary: Connect an existing domain to Convex and verify DNS, HTTPS, and sign-in settings.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: All three backtick alerts match Markdown formatting, not Ruby or shell command substitution. The workflow requires approval for DNS writes but does not explicitly require it before changing the Convex domain or sign-in origin. No evidence of prompt injection or credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Live Convex domain and sign-in changes lack an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the target deployment, domain, sign-in settings, and expected impact before requesting approval. Record the previous settings and verify sign-in after publishing.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format a Convex hostname pattern in Markdown. The surrounding text identifies a DNS target and does not instruct the agent to execute that pattern.

The backticks format provider CLI examples and do not invoke shell substitution. The workflow checks authentication with read-only commands and requires approval after showing the exact DNS write commands.
The backticks format a read-only dig lookup in Markdown. The lookup checks DNS records without modifying them or invoking command substitution.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Approval for Live Convex Configuration Changes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to attach the custom domain, change the sign-in origin, and redeploy without explicitly confirming those changes. Changing the wrong deployment or origin can interrupt sign-in.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The DNS step and rules explicitly require consent for DNS writes. The domain attachment and sign-in steps direct state changes but do not extend that requirement.

content.user_title: Connect a Custom Domain to Convex
content.value_statement: Connecting your own domain to Convex requires changes in both your DNS provider and your Convex deployment. This skill helps you plan those changes, verify HTTPS, and update sign-in settings.
actual_capabilities: Identify the published Convex site hostname or the deployment URL for HTTP actions.
List the routing and verification records to add at your DNS provider.
Check for an authenticated DNS CLI and offer to apply the records after approval.
Guide custom domain attachment and check whether the DNS records resolve.
Identify sign-in origin settings to update and verify HTTPS and any configured apex redirect.
limitations: You must already own the domain and have access to its DNS settings.
The skill does not install a DNS CLI, log in to one, or request registrar credentials.
Automatic DNS changes depend on a supported provider and an authenticated tool with write access.
DNS propagation can take minutes to hours.

use_cases.title: Publish a Site on a Custom Domain
use_cases.description: Identify the Convex hosting target and get the records to add in your DNS dashboard.

use_cases.title: Review DNS Changes Before Applying Them
use_cases.description: Confirm the DNS account, inspect the proposed changes, and verify the records after applying them.

use_cases.title: Plan a Domain Change for Sign-in
use_cases.description: Identify the origin settings to update and plan checks for sign-in after republishing.

prompt_templates.title: List Manual DNS Records
prompt_templates.scenario: You are setting up your first custom domain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect [domain] to my published Convex site using [DNS provider]. List the routing and verification records I need. Do not apply changes.

prompt_templates.title: Select the Convex Target
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a domain for HTTP actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me point [API hostname] at the HTTP actions URL for [deployment]. Explain which target to use and how to verify it after attachment.

prompt_templates.title: Review DNS Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Your DNS provider CLI is already authenticated.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check which account and DNS zone the existing [provider] CLI uses. Show the exact proposed changes for [hostname] and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Domain Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Your production app uses passkeys or OAuth.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the move from [old hostname] to [new hostname] for [production deployment]. Include DNS, domain attachment, sign-in origin changes, and HTTPS checks. Ask before applying or publishing changes.

output_examples.input: What should I do in my DNS dashboard for a new Convex site subdomain?
output_examples.output: Add a CNAME for the subdomain that points to the published Convex site hostname. Add the TXT record shown by Convex for ownership verification. Once both records resolve, check the custom domain status and test HTTPS.

output_examples.input: What should I review before my production app changes domains?
output_examples.output: Confirm the production deployment and new hostname before attaching the domain. Review the site URL and allowed origin, plus the relying party ID if the app uses passkeys. After republishing, test HTTPS and sign-in on the new domain.

best_practices: Confirm the DNS account, zone, hostname, and Convex deployment before approving changes.
Use the exact TXT verification host and value shown by Convex.
Verify DNS and HTTPS, then test sign-in when authentication is enabled.
anti_patterns: Sharing registrar credentials or API tokens in chat.
Adding only the routing record and skipping TXT ownership verification.
Changing a live sign-in origin without confirming the deployment and planning a sign-in test.

faq.question: Can I use a domain I already own?
faq.answer: Yes. You need access to its DNS settings and permission to configure the target Convex deployment.

faq.question: Does this work for Convex HTTP actions?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the deployment URL for HTTP actions instead of the published site hostname.

faq.question: Do I need a DNS CLI?
faq.answer: No. You can enter the routing and TXT verification records in your DNS provider dashboard.

faq.question: Can the skill change DNS records automatically?
faq.answer: It can offer to update records using a supported, authenticated tool. Review the proposed changes and approve them before they run.

faq.question: Why is my new domain not verified yet?
faq.answer: DNS propagation can take minutes to hours. Check that the routing record and TXT verification record resolve with the expected values.

faq.question: Will changing the domain affect sign-in?
faq.answer: It can for apps that use passkeys or OAuth. Review the origin settings, republish the app, and test sign-in on the new domain.
